Playbook.name: NETSCOUT AED — Surge in High-Confidence Threat Activity Against a Bank Internet Service - SOC Playbook

Reference.title: MITRE ATT and CK - T1190 Exploit Public-Facing Application

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: NETSCOUT Arbor Edge Defense reported a surge of high-confidence threat events - ATLAS threat categories "Botnet Command and Control", "Active Exploiters", "DNS Flood" (and cs7 "Command and Control") - against JCB internet-facing banking services. Triage question: is this a coordinated threat campaign / attempted exploitation reaching a bank service, or high-confidence reputation traffic that AED is blocking at the perimeter with no reach or impact?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: High-confidence AED categories such as active exploiters and botnet C2 targeting an internet-facing banking service represent the initial-access stage against the bank's exposed infrastructure. A source that reaches (is not blocked by) a real service, or a coordinated surge from many sources, can precede exploitation and a foothold.

Assets.AssetType: JCB internet-facing banking services behind NETSCOUT AED (bank range 91.223.202.0/24 - AED protection groups such as "Mena Mobile", "JCB Mobile ICS", "TEJARI WEBSITE", "NEW OWA ONPREM", "Middleware Prod", "Corporate Online")

LogSources.LogSource: NETSCOUT Arbor Edge Defense CEF - logs-cef.log-*

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: NETSCOUT AED CEF (verified live on JCB). Populated fields: source.ip, source.geo.country_name, source.as.organization.name, destination.ip, destination.port, network.transport, cef.name, cef.device.event_class_id, cef.extensions.deviceCustomString2 (protection group / bank service), cef.extensions.deviceCustomString6 (ATLAS threat category), cef.extensions.cs7 (ATLAS threat class, e.g. "Command and Control"), cef.severity.

High-confidence categories observed live on JCB: deviceCustomString6 in "Botnet Command and Control", "Active Exploiters", "DNS Flood" (also "MOVEit Transfer"/"CnC Other"/"Eleven11 Botnet" when present) and cs7 == "Command and Control". Perimeter caveat: AED sees inbound external sources hitting bank destinations - it does not show internal host beaconing. Endpoint/firewall telemetry is required to confirm any internal C2.

Signal.Name: Surge in High-Confidence Threat Activity
Signal.Details: A volume of high-confidence ATLAS threat events (botnet C2 / active exploiters / DNS flood) against a bank service above the rule threshold.

Input.name: $srcip
Input.description: Source IP flagged under a high-confidence threat category (source.ip - alert entity).

Input.name: $protgroup
Input.description: Bank service / AED protection group under threat (cef.extensions.deviceCustomString2). Used to measure the campaign scope against the service.

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the full evidence story per the ClassificationGuidance - the threat category, whether the source reached (vs was blocked by) a real bank service, and whether it is one source or a coordinated surge - not any single fact. "Active Exploiters" reaching a live service is far more serious than a blocked reputation hit.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the high-confidence threat surge is real attacker activity reaching JCB banking services (which categories, which assets, whether blocked, and whether it is a coordinated campaign) versus perimeter-blocked reputation traffic.

Step.name: Threat categories and assets for the source
Step.Purpose: Establish what the source is flagged as (Botnet C2 / Active Exploiters / DNS Flood / cs7 Command and Control), against which bank services and assets, its volume and origin.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE observer.vendor == "NETSCOUT" AND source.ip == "$srcip" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS events = COUNT(*), threat_cats = VALUES(cef.extensions.deviceCustomString6), cs7 = VALUES(cef.extensions.cs7), classes = VALUES(cef.device.event_class_id), services = VALUES(cef.extensions.deviceCustomString2), dst_ips = VALUES(destination.ip), country = VALUES(source.geo.country_name), asn = VALUES(source.as.organization.name) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: "Active Exploiters" / "Botnet Command and Control" / cs7 "Command and Control" are the highest-value categories - attempted exploitation or C2 against a bank service. Check whether $srcip is external (expected - AED is a perimeter device) or, unusually, a bank-range address (91.223.202.0/24); a bank-range source would imply an internal compromised host and must be corroborated on endpoint/firewall telemetry (AED alone will not show internal beaconing).

Step.name: Bank assets, ports and whether the source was blocked
Step.Purpose: The specific destination IPs, services and ports the source hit, and the AED detection class (blocked vs reached), show real exposure and reach.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE observer.vendor == "NETSCOUT" AND source.ip == "$srcip" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS hits = COUNT(*), ports = VALUES(destination.port), transports = VALUES(network.transport), classes = VALUES(cef.device.event_class_id), names = VALUES(cef.name), cats = VALUES(cef.extensions.deviceCustomString6) BY destination.ip, cef.extensions.deviceCustomString2 | SORT hits DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: cef.name/class of "Blocked Host" means AED blocked it at the perimeter (mitigated). Any indication the source reached a live service, or repeated attempts against a real, exposed banking service/port, raises priority. Map the destination.ip / protection group to the actual service and confirm its exposure and patch state.

Step.name: Campaign scope against the bank service
Step.Purpose: Whether this source is one of many high-confidence threats hitting the same bank service establishes a coordinated surge/campaign versus an isolated source.
Step.Query: FROM logs-cef.log-* | WHERE observer.vendor == "NETSCOUT" AND cef.extensions.deviceCustomString2 == "$protgroup" AND (cef.extensions.deviceCustomString6 IN ("Botnet Command and Control","Active Exploiters","MOVEit Transfer","CnC Other","Eleven11 Botnet","DNS Flood") OR cef.extensions.cs7 == "Command and Control") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS events = COUNT(*), distinct_sources = COUNT_DISTINCT(source.ip), countries = COUNT_DISTINCT(source.geo.country_name), cats = VALUES(cef.extensions.deviceCustomString6) BY cef.extensions.deviceCustomString2 | LIMIT 5
Step.AnalystNotes: Many distinct high-confidence sources across many countries against one bank service = a coordinated campaign (elevate). A single source is an isolated attempt. Grounding: live JCB shows "Active Exploiters" activity spread across bank services (Mena Mobile, TEJARI WEBSITE, JCB Mobile ICS, NEW OWA ONPREM), typically one event per external source - a broad reputation-driven surge that AED blocks.

Node.Condition: A source flagged "Active Exploiters" / "Botnet Command and Control" / cs7 "Command and Control" reached (was not blocked by) a real bank service, or a coordinated surge of many high-confidence sources is hitting one service.
Node.Result: True Positive (Threat Campaign / attempted exploitation reaching a bank service - escalate)

Node.Condition: A bank-range (91.223.202.0/24) address appears as the source of C2 activity.
Node.Result: True Positive (Compromised internal host / C2 - corroborate on endpoint and hand to IR)

Node.Condition: High-confidence reputation events fully blocked by AED at the perimeter, no reach to a live service and no coordinated surge - or an authorised security assessment.
Node.Result: False Positive (proven-blocked reputation traffic, or authorised assessment)

Node.Condition: High-confidence activity against a bank service where reach, exposure or campaign scope cannot be established from available telemetry.

FalsePositive.Definition: An authorised assessment OR proven-blocked high-confidence reputation traffic that AED mitigated at the perimeter with no reach or impact. Never classify simply as "benign".

Indicators.Item: Every event is "Blocked Host" at the perimeter; no reach to a live service.
Isolated source(s), no coordinated surge, low volume against a given service.
Activity maps to an authorised penetration test / security scan window.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the blocks held / the authorised assessment; document; close as proven-blocked or authorised. Add notable source IPs/ASNs to blocklists and threat hunting.

TruePositive.Definition: Real high-confidence threat activity against JCB banking services: attempted exploitation or C2 reaching a service, a coordinated campaign, or an internal host acting as a C2 source.

Indicators.Item: "Active Exploiters" / "Botnet Command and Control" / cs7 "Command and Control" against a real, exposed bank service.
A surge of many distinct high-confidence sources across countries against one service (coordinated campaign).
Any bank-range IP appearing as a C2 source (internal compromise), or evidence the source reached a live service.

SOCAction.Item: If a bank-range source or a reached service is present: treat as an intrusion - endpoint IR on the internal host and/or verify the exposed service is patched and not compromised. Otherwise: blocklist the sources/ASNs, confirm AED blocking, and hunt for follow-on activity across WAF/firewall/endpoint telemetry.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Identify the threat categories and whether $srcip is external or a bank-range address (INV-01). A bank-range C2 source is an internal compromise - escalate to endpoint IR immediately.
Determine whether the source reached or was blocked, and which real bank services/ports were targeted (INV-02).
Assess campaign scope against the service (INV-03) - one source vs a coordinated surge.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: For internal C2 sources: endpoint IR on the host and correlate with endpoint/firewall telemetry. For inbound threats: blocklist sources/ASNs, confirm AED blocking, and verify the targeted services are patched and not compromised.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Tune AED threat categories; integrate high-confidence threat IPs/ASNs into perimeter blocklists and endpoint hunting; reduce exposure of targeted services; document the campaign.

Escalation.Trigger: A bank-range C2 source (internal compromise), a high-confidence source that reached a live bank service, or a coordinated multi-source campaign against a banking service.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Proven-blocked reputation traffic or authorised assessment confirmed; no reach and no campaign; notable sources blocklisted; documented.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Internal C2 host IR'd and/or targeted services confirmed patched and uncompromised; sources/ASNs blocklisted; AED blocking confirmed; campaign correlated across telemetry and documented for hunting.
